## 5.1

By the chain rule of probability, the joint density factors as
$$
f_{X_{0:N}}(x_{0:N})
= f_{X_0}(x_0) \prod_{n=1}^{N} f_{X_n \mid X_0, \ldots, X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_0, \ldots, x_{n-1})
$$
Since $(X_n)$ is a Markov process, the future is conditionally independent of the past given the present:
$$
f_{X_n \mid X_0, \ldots, X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_0, \ldots, x_{n-1})
= f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1}), \quad n = 1, \ldots, N
$$
Therefore, we derive the joint distribution as
$$
f_{X_{0:N}}(x_{0:N})
= f_{X_0}(x_0) \prod_{n=1}^{N} f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1}) \qquad \blacksquare
$$

## 5.2

Applying the marginalization identity $f_{X \mid Y} = \int f_{X, Z \mid Y}\, dz$ with $X = X_n$, $Z = X_{n-1}$, $Y = Y_{1:n-1}$, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})
&= \int f_{X_n,\, X_{n-1} \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n, x_{n-1} \mid y_{1:n-1})\, dx_{n-1} \\
&= \int f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1},\, Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1}, y_{1:n-1})\,
   f_{X_{n-1} \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_{n-1} \mid y_{1:n-1})\, dx_{n-1}
\end{aligned}
$$
Since $(X_n)$ is Markov and $Y_k$ depends only on $X_k$, we have $X_n \perp Y_{1:n-1} \mid X_{n-1}$,
$$
f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1},\, Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1}, y_{1:n-1})
= f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1}).
$$
Thus we derive the prediction formula
$$
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})
= \int f_{X_{n-1} \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_{n-1} \mid y_{1:n-1})\,
  f_{X_n \mid X_{n-1}}(x_n \mid x_{n-1})\, dx_{n-1} \qquad \blacksquare
$$

## 5.3

From the definition of conditional density and the product rule $f_{X,Y\mid Z} = f_{Y \mid X, Z}\, f_{X \mid Z}$, we can write
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n})
&= \frac{f_{X_n,\, Y_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n, y_n \mid y_{1:n-1})}
        {f_{Y_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid y_{1:n-1})} \\
&= \frac{f_{Y_n \mid X_n,\, Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid x_n, y_{1:n-1})\,
         f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})}
        {f_{Y_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid y_{1:n-1})}
\end{aligned}
$$
In a POMP model the measurement $Y_n$ depends on the latent state only through $X_n$, so $Y_n \perp Y_{1:n-1} \mid X_n$. Therefore:
$$
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n})
= \frac{f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})\,
        f_{Y_n \mid X_n}(y_n \mid x_n)}
       {f_{Y_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid y_{1:n-1})} \qquad \blacksquare
$$
This is the filtering formula.

To compute the conditional likelihood formula, we apply the marginalization identity $f_{X \mid Y} = \int f_{X, Z \mid Y}\, dz$ with $X = Y_n$, $Z = X_n$, $Y = Y_{1:n-1}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{Y_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid y_{1:n-1})
&= \int f_{Y_n,\, X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n, x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})\, dx_n \\
&= \int f_{Y_n \mid X_n,\, Y_{1:n-1}}(y_n \mid x_n, y_{1:n-1})\,
       f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})\, dx_n \\
&= \int f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})\,
       f_{Y_n \mid X_n}(y_n \mid x_n)\, dx_n \qquad \blacksquare
\end{aligned}
$$
The last equation is implied from the POMP measurement model.

## 5.4

Write $Y_{n:N} = (Y_n, Y_{n+1:N})$ and apply the product rule $f_{X,Y\mid Z} = f_{X\mid Z}\,f_{Y\mid X,Z}$, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{Y_{n:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n:N}\mid x_n)
&= f_{Y_n \mid X_n}(y_n \mid x_n)\,
   f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n,\,Y_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n, y_n)
\end{aligned}
$$
Under the measurement model assumption,
$$
f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n,\,Y_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n, y_n)
= f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n),
$$
so
$$
f_{Y_{n:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n:N}\mid x_n)
= f_{Y_n\mid X_n}(y_n\mid x_n)\,
  f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n) \qquad \blacksquare
$$

Let $Z = X_{n+1}$ and apply $f_{X\mid Y} = \int f_{X,Z\mid Y}\,dz$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n)
&= \int f_{Y_{n+1:N},\,X_{n+1}\mid X_n}(y_{n+1:N}, x_{n+1}\mid x_n)\,dx_{n+1} \\
&= \int f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_{n+1},\,X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_{n+1}, x_n)\,
       f_{X_{n+1}\mid X_n}(x_{n+1}\mid x_n)\,dx_{n+1}
\end{aligned}
$$
By the Markov property, $Y_{n+1:N} \perp X_n \mid X_{n+1}$, so
$$
f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_{n+1},\,X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_{n+1}, x_n)
= f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_{n+1}}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_{n+1})
$$
Hence the final derivation is
$$
f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_n}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_n)
= \int f_{Y_{n+1:N}\mid X_{n+1}}(y_{n+1:N}\mid x_{n+1})\,
       f_{X_{n+1}\mid X_n}(x_{n+1}\mid x_n)\,dx_{n+1} \qquad \blacksquare
$$

## 5.5


Split $Y_{1:N} = (Y_{1:n-1}, Y_{n:N})$ and apply Bayes' rule, we have
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:N}}(x_n \mid y_{1:N})
&= f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1},\, Y_{n:N}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1}, y_{n:N}) \\[4pt]
&= \frac{f_{Y_{n:N} \mid X_n,\, Y_{1:n-1}}(y_{n:N} \mid x_n, y_{1:n-1})\,
         f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})}
        {f_{Y_{n:N} \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_{n:N} \mid y_{1:n-1})}
\end{aligned}
$$
In a POMP model the current state $X_n$ renders future observations $Y_{n:N}$ independent of the past $Y_{1:n-1}$. Therefore:
$$
f_{Y_{n:N} \mid X_n,\, Y_{1:n-1}}(y_{n:N} \mid x_n, y_{1:n-1})
= f_{Y_{n:N} \mid X_n}(y_{n:N} \mid x_n)
$$
Substituting gives the final smoothing formula
$$
f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:N}}(x_n \mid y_{1:N})
= \frac{f_{X_n \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(x_n \mid y_{1:n-1})\,
        f_{Y_{n:N} \mid X_n}(y_{n:N} \mid x_n)}
       {f_{Y_{n:N} \mid Y_{1:n-1}}(y_{n:N} \mid y_{1:n-1})} \qquad \blacksquare
$$
